problems.title: Adding identity transitions can accelerate mixing
claim: The paper states that \((I+A)/2\) preserves stationary state and slows convergence because of increased self-transition.
analysis: Take positive stochastic attention \(A=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}.1&.9\\.9&.1\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), realizable by finite logits \(Q=I,K=\sqrt2(\log A)^T\). Its nontrivial eigenvalue is \(-.8\); the lazy chain has \(.1\). From a single-state start, total variation to \((1/2,1/2)\) is \((.8)^k/2\) versus \((.1)^k/2\). Thus identity addition accelerates this already aperiodic chain. Stationary-distribution preservation remains valid.
result: The unrestricted mixing-direction explanation is false. TokenRank and reported empirical improvements are not thereby refuted.
repair: State the eigenvalue map \(\lambda\mapsto(1+\lambda)/2\); mixing direction depends on the spectrum. A reversible nonnegative-spectrum restriction supports the narrower spectral-slowdown statement.
problems.impact_rationale: This corrects an explanatory spectral claim, while the core stationary-chain construction survives.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Eigenvalue modulus does not certify metastable regions
problems.source_location: Sections 3.1/4.4; Supplement E.1; dino.py eigenvalue weighting
claim: The magnitude of the second eigenvalue is associated with stable metastable regions and used for head weighting.
analysis: Positive stochastic matrices with diagonal entries \(.99\) or \(.01\), respectively, have nontrivial eigenvalues \(.98\) and \(-.98\), hence identical modulus. In a two-state chain, expected singleton residence time is \(1/(1-A_{ii})\): \(100\) for the first, only \(1/.99\) for the second. Large negative modulus describes persistent alternation rather than prolonged residence; the scalar also loses multiplicity information.
result: Modulus alone neither certifies nor counts metastable regions. The measured weighting correlation can still hold for observed attention heads; their negative-mode frequency is unmeasured.
repair: Present modulus as an empirical spectral feature; stronger semantic-metastability claims require structural assumptions and retention/exit measurements.
problems.impact_rationale: The unsupported interpretation is broader than the empirical head-weighting evidence, which is not contradicted.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Nonuniform personalization breaks row stochasticity
claim: The helper promises a stochastic personalized transition but uses \(E=ee^T/n\).
analysis: For \(A=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}.8&.2\\.3&.7\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), \(\alpha=.8\) and probability vector \(e=(.75,.25)^T\), the returned row sums are \(.875\) and \(.825\). Generally they equal \(\alpha+(1-\alpha)e_i\sum_je_j/n\), not one. Normalizing later power iterates produces a different Perron iteration, not a stochastic matrix. The default all-ones branch is valid.
result: The optional personalized release branch violates its contract. No evidence shows published demos used that branch.
repair: For normalized positive \(p\), use \(T=\alpha A+(1-\alpha)\mathbf1p^T\). Rows sum to one; positivity gives ergodicity. Zero entries in \(p\) need additional assumptions for that stronger guarantee.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a local optional-branch defect; the paper’s uniform teleportation formula and default experiments are not shown affected.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

impact_rationale: Minor: local explanatory overclaims and an optional release branch fail, without demonstrated damage to TokenRank’s core construction or empirical benefits.
